chapter.title: Chapter 2: Object Oriented System Analysis and Design (OOSAD) 📚

content.subtitle: Abstraction 🔍
content.description: Process of extracting essential characteristics, ignoring irrelevant details. Classifies phenomena into concepts, enabling complexity management.

items.definition: Person in University vs. Police system; Cat vs. Temperature sensor.
Entity (domain model), Action (operations), Virtual machine (grouped operations), Coincidental (unrelated operations).

content.subtitle: Encapsulation 🔒
content.description: Hides state details, associating behavior with data. Compartmentalizes implementation, acting as a black box.

content.subtitle: Information Hiding 🕵️
content.description: Achieved through encapsulation, separating interface from implementation.

content.subtitle: Inheritance 🌳
content.description: Allows objects to be built from other objects, supporting hierarchical classification and reusability.

content.subtitle: Association 🔗
content.description: Binary relationship between classes, describing activities.

content.subtitle: Aggregation 🗂️
content.description: Represents 'has-a' relationship, where a class is composed of other objects.

content.subtitle: Persistence 💾
content.description: Ensures objects are available for future use by saving attributes and relationships to storage.

content.subtitle: Coupling and Cohesion ⚖️
content.description: Modularity implies cohesive, loosely coupled components.

content.subtitle: Polymorphism 🦋
content.description: Operation exhibits different behaviors based on data types.

content.subtitle: Interfaces 📜
content.description: Collection of methods/attributes defining cohesive behaviors, implemented by classes.

content.subtitle: Components 🧩
content.description: Modular, extensible units with specified interfaces and dependencies.

content.subtitle: Overview 📋
content.description: Framework for planning and managing software development, dividing work into phases.

content.subtitle: Phases of SDLC 📊
content.description: Typically five stages, sometimes expanded to seven.

items.definition: Planning, Feasibility/Requirements Analysis, Design/Prototyping, Development, Testing, Implementation/Integration, Operations/Maintenance.
Creates working models for requirement verification; Throwaway or Evolutionary.
Builds successive versions, refining requirements each iteration.
Risk-oriented, combines Waterfall and prototyping, not suited for small projects.
Focuses on faster development using CASE tools and prototypes.
Adaptive, lightweight, emphasizes people and working software.

content.subtitle: Overview 📝
content.description: Iterative, incremental methodology using UML models, adaptable to specific systems.

items.definition: Determines economic viability, produces initial models and plans.
Ensures client requirements are met, finalizes artifacts.

content.subtitle: Definition 📜
content.description: Graphical notation for describing and designing software systems, particularly object-oriented.

items.definition: Provides precise models for analysis and design.
Structural (Class, Interface, etc.), Behavioral (Interaction, State Machine), Grouping (Packages), Annotational (Notes).
Use Case, Sequence, Collaboration, State Chart, Activity.
Shows system usage with actors, use cases, and relationships (Association, Generalization, Extend, Include).
Depicts step-by-step workflows, showing control flow with actions and decisions.
Models control flow by time, showing object interactions and messages.
Shows classes, attributes, methods, and relationships (Association, Aggregation, Generalization).

content.subtitle: Overview 🌐
content.description: UML supports modeling for system analysis, design, and deployment, providing standardized notation for visualizing and documenting software systems.
